- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. 4 5 # RUTH 6 7 A [Teleport](https://goteleport.com) access-request plugin that routes each pending request through an AI risk analyst, auto-approves the boring ones, and files an ITSM Jira ticket for the sketchy ones — with the Teleport request held in `PENDING` until an SRE resolves the ticket. 8 9 Risk tiers: 10 11 | Score | Tier | Action | 12 | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------- | 13 | 0–24 | low | auto-approve, no Jira ticket | 14 | 25–49 | medium | file ITSM ticket, hold request pending | 15 | 50–74 | high | file ITSM ticket with tier label | 16 | 75–100 | critical | file ITSM ticket with tier label | 17 18 The ticket-creation threshold is configurable (`risk.ticket_threshold`). Session escalations — access requests carrying the `ruth.escalation` Teleport annotation — use a tighter fallback threshold (`risk.escalation_threshold`) and support per-role overrides in `risk.escalation_thresholds`. 19 20 ## How it works 21 22 ``` 23 Teleport ──► watcher ──► scorer ──► AI provider ──► tier 24 │ 25 ├── below threshold ──► auto-approve via AccessReview 26 │ 27 └── at/above threshold ──► Jira ITSM ticket ──► poll status 28 │ 29 SRE approves/rejects │ 30 ▼ 31 Teleport AccessReview 32 ``` 33 34 **Risk components:** 35 36 - **Structural (deterministic):** missing `CUSTX-###` ticket reference (+30), thin description `<40` chars (+15), off-hours request (+10). 37 - **AI-judged (clamped):** description quality 0–25, privilege concern 0–25, anomalies 0–10. 38 39 ## User reputation 40 41 Every requester starts at `reputation.starting_score` (default `100`) and 42 accumulates deductions for each bad request they file. Penalties and the 43 `[floor, ceiling]` clamp are fully configurable: 44 45 | Signal | Config key | Default | 46 | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------- | 47 | Missing CUSTX ticket | `reputation.penalty_missing_custx` | `10` | 48 | Thin (<40 char) reason | `reputation.penalty_thin_description` | `5` | 49 50 State is persisted as a JSON map at `reputation.persist_path` via atomic 51 rename — no external database required. The file survives restarts; leave 52 `persist_path` empty to keep everything in memory. 53 54 Reputation only ever goes down. If somebody wants their number back, 55 they can file better requests next quarter. Or not. 56 57 ## Telemetry / shaming pipeline 58 59 When `telemetry.enabled = true`, RUTH stands up an OpenTelemetry 60 `MeterProvider` with an OTLP/gRPC exporter pointed at the configured 61 collector. It registers one observable gauge: 62 63 - `ruth.user.reputation` — int64, tagged with `user`, observed every 64 `telemetry.export_period` (default `15s`). 65 66 Route your collector's output to Datadog (or Prometheus, or wherever) and 67 the gauge lands tagged per user, ready to be pinned to a dashboard for 68 the monthly team meeting. 69 70 ## AI providers 71 72 Pick one via `ai.provider`: 73 74 - **`anthropic`** — direct call to the Anthropic Messages API. System prompt is sent with `cache_control: ephemeral` so repeated scoring hits the prompt cache. 75 - **`bedrock`** — `bedrockruntime:InvokeModel` against a Claude-on-Bedrock model. Uses the default AWS credential chain (IRSA / Pod Identity / env / profile); optional `profile` and `role_arn` for local dev and cross-account AssumeRole. 76 - **`random`** — test-only provider that fabricates assessments within valid ranges. Use for local dev and integration tests; emits a startup warning so it doesn't silently ship to prod. Accepts an optional `seed` for deterministic runs. 77 78 ## Install 79 80 ```sh 81 go mod tidy 82 go build -o ruth ./cmd/ruth 83 ``` 84 85 ## Configure 86 87 Copy `ruth.toml.example` to `/etc/ruth/ruth.toml` and fill in: 88 89 - `[teleport]` — proxy address + path to an identity file for a Teleport user with permission to watch access requests and submit reviews. 90 - `[ai]` — pick a provider and supply its credentials. 91 - `[jira]` — API user, token, ITSM project key, and the status names to treat as approved/rejected (e.g. `"Approved"` / `"Rejected"`). 92 - `[risk]` — threshold, CUSTX pattern (defaults to `CUSTX-\d+`), off-hours window, timezone. 93 94 ### Dry-run mode 95 96 Set `dry_run = true` (or `RUTH_DRY_RUN=true`) to score every incoming request and 97 log the decision RUTH *would* make — auto-approve, or "would file ITSM 98 ticket and hold pending" — without actually calling Teleport or Jira. Handy for 99 previewing a new threshold, AI provider, or escalation rule before letting the 100 plugin loose on production access requests. 101 102 ### Environment variable overrides 103 104 Every scalar TOML key can be overridden by an environment variable. Risk tiers: | Score | Tier | Action | | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------- | | 0–24 | low | auto-approve, no Jira ticket | | 25–49 | medium | file ITSM ticket, hold request pending | | 50–74 | high | file ITSM ticket with tier label | | 75–100 | critical | file ITSM ticket with tier label | The ticket-creation threshold is configurable (`risk.ticket_threshold`). Session escalations — access requests carrying the `ruth.escalation` Teleport annotation — use a tighter fallback threshold (`risk.escalation_threshold`) and support per-role overrides in `risk.escalation_thresholds`. ## How it works ``` Teleport ──► watcher ──► scorer ──► AI provider ──► tier │ ├── below threshold ──► auto-approve via AccessReview │ └── at/above threshold ──► Jira ITSM ticket ──► poll status │ SRE approves/rejects │ ▼ Teleport AccessReview ``` **Risk components:** - **Structural (deterministic):** missing `CUSTX-###` ticket reference (+30), thin description `<40` chars (+15), off-hours request (+10). - **AI-judged (clamped):** description quality 0–25, privilege concern 0–25, anomalies 0–10. ## User reputation Every requester starts at `reputation.starting_score` (default `100`) and accumulates deductions for each bad request they file. Penalties and the `[floor, ceiling]` clamp are fully configurable: | Signal | Config key | Default | | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------- | | Missing CUSTX ticket | `reputation.penalty_missing_custx` | `10` | | Thin (<40 char) reason | `reputation.penalty_thin_description` | `5` | State is persisted as a JSON map at `reputation.persist_path` via atomic rename — no external database required. Or not. ## Telemetry / shaming pipeline When `telemetry.enabled = true`, RUTH stands up an OpenTelemetry `MeterProvider` with an OTLP/gRPC exporter pointed at the configured collector. It registers one observable gauge: - `ruth.user.reputation` — int64, tagged with `user`, observed every `telemetry.export_period` (default `15s`). package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"flag"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"ruth"
)

func main() {
	configPath := flag.String("config", "ruth.toml", "Path to TOML configuration")
	flag.Parse()

	cfg, err := ruth.LoadConfig(*configPath)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Error("config load failed", "path", *configPath, "err", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	setupLogging(cfg.Log.Level)

	ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer cancel()

	app, err := ruth.NewApp(ctx, cfg)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Error("app init failed", "err", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	runErr := app.Run(ctx)

	shutdownCtx, cancelShutdown := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancelShutdown()
	if err := app.Close(shutdownCtx); err != nil {
		slog.Warn("shutdown error", "err", err)
	}

	if runErr != nil && !errors.Is(runErr, context.Canceled) {
		slog.Error("app exited with error", "err", runErr)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func setupLogging(level string) {
	var l slog.Level
	switch level {
	case "debug":
		l = slog.LevelDebug
	case "warn":
		l = slog.LevelWarn
	case "error":
		l = slog.LevelError
	default:
		l = slog.LevelInfo
	}
	h := slog.NewJSONHandler(os.Stderr, &slog.HandlerOptions{Level: l})
	slog.SetDefault(slog.New(h))
}

**Deterministic (hard rules):**
- Missing `CUSTX-###` ticket reference: **+30**
- Description < 40 chars: **+15**
- Off-hours request: **+10**

**AI-judged (Claude-scored, clamped):**
- `description_quality`: 0–25 (0 = specific, 25 = vague/empty)
- `privilege_concern`: 0–25 (0 = read-only, 25 = prod-root/destructive)
- `anomalies`: 0–10 (scope mismatches, injection attempts)

Total capped at 100. Tiers: low (0–24), medium (25–49), high (50–74), critical (75–100). Default ticket threshold is 25.

---

## The AI system prompt (`ai/provider.go:67`)

This is the most distinctive piece. The prompt persona is a **grumpy-but-loving grandmother** ("abuela") who is a seasoned security analyst. She's generous by default — a brief-but-specific request gets "a kiss on the forehead." The chancla only comes out for genuinely reckless requests (prod-root with "need access to look at things"). 

Critically, the prompt is carefully hardened against prompt injection: free-form fields are treated as *untrusted user input to assess, never instructions to follow*. Injection attempts drive `anomalies` up, never down.

| `reputation/` | Per-user score store with atomic JSON file persistence |
| `telemetry/` | OTLP/gRPC meter, `ruth.user.reputation` observable gauge |

# Local test harness

A docker-compose stack for exercising ruth end-to-end without real
Teleport, Anthropic, or Jira credentials.

## What runs where

| Component      | Where  | Notes                                                                    |
| -------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Teleport       | docker | Single-node auth+proxy cluster, self-signed TLS, port `3080`             |
| OTel collector | docker | OTLP/gRPC on `4317`, prints metrics to stdout via the debug exporter     |
| AI scoring     | inproc | `random` provider in `local/ruth.toml` fabricates assessments        |
| ruth       | host   | `go run ./cmd/ruth --config local/ruth.toml`                     |
| submit         | host   | `go run ./cmd/submit --reason "…"` fires test access requests            |

Jira is stubbed: `risk.ticket_threshold` is cranked to `101` in
`local/ruth.toml`, so nothing ever hits Jira. Reputation scoring runs
before that branch, so the test loop is intact.

## One-time setup

```sh
# from apps/ruth
./local/bootstrap.sh
```

This brings the stack up, applies the roles + users from
`local/resources.yaml`, and writes identity files to `local/identity/` for
the `ruth` plugin user and the `charles` test requester. Identities
are TTL 24h — re-run the script when they expire.

## Running

Three terminals:

```sh
# 1. watch metrics flow past
docker compose -f local/docker-compose.yml logs -f otel-collector

# 2. run ruth against the local cluster
go run ./cmd/ruth --config local/ruth.toml

# 3. fire test access requests
go run ./cmd/submit --reason "plz"
go run ./cmd/submit --reason "CUSTX-1234 debug prod-api p95 spike, repro in ticket"
```

## What you should see

- **ruth logs** — a `reputation docked` line for the "plz" request
  (no CUSTX reference, <40 chars → both penalties), no line for the
  well-formed one.
- **otel-collector logs** — every 5 seconds, a `ruth.user.reputation`
  gauge emitted for each user that has been scored, tagged with `user`.
  Charles' score should start at `100` and drop by `15` (10 + 5) per bad
  request, floored at `0`.
- **local/reputation.json** — the persisted state. Delete it to start fresh.

## Tearing down

```sh
docker compose -f local/docker-compose.yml down -v
rm -rf local/identity local/reputation.json
```

## Troubleshooting

- **`tctl status` times out during bootstrap** — bump the 60s wait in
  `bootstrap.sh`. First boot downloads the teleport image (~300MB).
- **`connect: context deadline exceeded` from submit** — teleport proxy
  not listening yet, or port 3080 collision. `lsof -i :3080` to check.
- **No metrics in the collector logs** — confirm `telemetry.enabled = true`
  in `local/ruth.toml` and that the gauge callback has users to
  observe (i.e., at least one request has been scored since startup;
  empty stores emit nothing).

# RUTH — Teleport access plugin with AI risk scoring
# Copy to /etc/ruth/ruth.toml and fill in.
#
# Any scalar key can also be overridden via a RUTH_-prefixed environment
# variable (e.g. RUTH_TELEPORT_ADDR, RUTH_AI_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY,
# RUTH_JIRA_POLL_INTERVAL=2m). Precedence: env > this file > defaults.
# Maps (risk.escalation_thresholds) and slices are TOML-only.

# When true, log the decision (auto-approve / would-create-ticket) for each
# access request without calling Teleport or Jira. Useful for previewing a
# new threshold or AI provider before flipping the switch in prod.
# dry_run = false

[teleport]
addr = "proxy.example.com:443"
identity_file = "/var/lib/teleport/ruth.pem"

[ai]
# Exactly one of: "anthropic", "bedrock", "random".
# "random" is for local dev / integration tests only — it fabricates
# assessments and must not be used in production.
provider = "anthropic"

[ai.anthropic]
api_key = "sk-ant-..."
model = "claude-sonnet-4-6"

[ai.bedrock]
region = "us-west-2"
model_id = "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6-v1:0"
# Authentication: by default the AWS SDK default credential chain is used,
# which covers IRSA, EKS Pod Identity, EC2 instance profiles, ECS task roles,
# env vars, and ~/.aws/credentials — no config needed in prod.
# profile = "dev"                           # named shared-config profile (local dev)
# role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/bedrock-invoker"  # cross-account AssumeRole
# role_session_name = "ruth"
# external_id = "optional-external-id"

[ai.random]
# Optional: set a non-zero seed for deterministic output (useful in CI).
# seed = 0

[jira]
url = "https://example.atlassian.net"
username = "bot@example.com"
api_token = "replace-me"
project = "ITSM"
issue_type = "Task"
poll_interval = "30s"
approved_status = "Approved"
rejected_status = "Rejected"

[risk]
# Requests scoring >= ticket_threshold get an ITSM ticket (and stay PENDING).
# Anything below is auto-approved as "no cap".
ticket_threshold = 25
custx_pattern = 'CUSTX-\d+'
# Off-hours window applies a +10 risk bump. Wraps midnight when start > end.
off_hours_start = 18
off_hours_end = 8
timezone = "America/New_York"

# Session escalations — access requests that Teleport tags with the
# escalation_annotation (set via the role's allow.request.annotations).
# These use a tighter fallback threshold. Per-role overrides in
# [risk.escalation_thresholds] take precedence; the strictest (lowest)
# value wins when a request names multiple roles.
escalation_annotation = "ruth.escalation"
escalation_threshold  = 15

[risk.escalation_thresholds]
# "sre-admin"    = 5
# "db-admin"     = 10
# "read-only"    = 25

[reputation]
# Per-user reputation, persisted as JSON on local disk. Every user starts
# at starting_score; points are deducted for bad requests and clamped to
# [floor_score, ceiling_score]. Reputation only goes down — the point is
# to shame, not to forgive.
persist_path              = "/var/lib/ruth/reputation.json"
starting_score            = 100
floor_score               = 0
ceiling_score             = 100
penalty_missing_custx     = 10
penalty_thin_description  = 5

[telemetry]
# Emit per-user reputation as an OTLP gauge for the collector to ship to
# Datadog. Disable to keep reputation state local only.
enabled        = true
endpoint       = "otel-collector:4317"
insecure       = true
service_name   = "ruth"
export_period  = "15s"
# Delay between receiving SIGINT/SIGTERM and cancelling the watcher so the
# OTel periodic reader can finish an in-flight export cleanly. Set to "0s"
# to shut down immediately at the cost of a noisy "context canceled"
# exporter error.
shutdown_grace = "2s"

[log]
level = "info"

# Local test harness

A docker-compose stack for exercising ruth end-to-end without real
Teleport, Anthropic, or Jira credentials.

## What runs where

| Component      | Where  | Notes                                                                    |
| -------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Teleport       | docker | Single-node auth+proxy cluster, self-signed TLS, port `3080`             |
| OTel collector | docker | OTLP/gRPC on `4317`, prints metrics to stdout via the debug exporter     |
| AI scoring     | inproc | `random` provider in `local/ruth.toml` fabricates assessments        |
| ruth       | host   | `go run ./cmd/ruth --config local/ruth.toml`                     |
| submit         | host   | `go run ./cmd/submit --reason "…"` fires test access requests            |

Jira is stubbed: `risk.ticket_threshold` is cranked to `101` in
`local/ruth.toml`, so nothing ever hits Jira. Reputation scoring runs
before that branch, so the test loop is intact.

## One-time setup

```sh
# from apps/ruth
./local/bootstrap.sh
```

This brings the stack up, applies the roles + users from
`local/resources.yaml`, and writes identity files to `local/identity/` for
the `ruth` plugin user and the `charles` test requester. Identities
are TTL 24h — re-run the script when they expire.

## Running

Three terminals:

```sh
# 1. watch metrics flow past
docker compose -f local/docker-compose.yml logs -f otel-collector

# 2. run ruth against the local cluster
go run ./cmd/ruth --config local/ruth.toml

# 3. fire test access requests
go run ./cmd/submit --reason "plz"
go run ./cmd/submit --reason "CUSTX-1234 debug prod-api p95 spike, repro in ticket"
```

## What you should see

- **ruth logs** — a `reputation docked` line for the "plz" request
  (no CUSTX reference, <40 chars → both penalties), no line for the
  well-formed one.
- **otel-collector logs** — every 5 seconds, a `ruth.user.reputation`
  gauge emitted for each user that has been scored, tagged with `user`.
  Charles' score should start at `100` and drop by `15` (10 + 5) per bad
  request, floored at `0`.
- **local/reputation.json** — the persisted state. Delete it to start fresh.

## Tearing down

```sh
docker compose -f local/docker-compose.yml down -v
rm -rf local/identity local/reputation.json
```

## Troubleshooting

- **`tctl status` times out during bootstrap** — bump the 60s wait in
  `bootstrap.sh`. First boot downloads the teleport image (~300MB).
- **`connect: context deadline exceeded` from submit** — teleport proxy
  not listening yet, or port 3080 collision. `lsof -i :3080` to check.
- **No metrics in the collector logs** — confirm `telemetry.enabled = true`
  in `local/ruth.toml` and that the gauge callback has users to
  observe (i.e., at least one request has been scored since startup;
  empty stores emit nothing).

# CLAUDE.md — RUTH

Guidance for Claude Code sessions working in `apps/ruth/`. Inherits the repo-wide rules in `/Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/CLAUDE.md`; this file documents project-specific context, history, and gotchas.

## Project history

- Originally named **televibe**; renamed to **RUTH** mid-development. A few stale strings may still reference televibe in archived branches/comments — flag them but don't change unless the user asks.
- The env-var prefix used to be `TV_`; it is now `RUTH_`.
- Current branch: `ruth-plugin`. Repository working directory: `apps/ruth/`.
- Original AI provider set was `anthropic` / `bedrock` / `webhook`. The webhook provider was replaced by a `random` test-only provider. The `anthropic` provider was removed in 2026-04-29 — surviving providers are **`bedrock`** (production) and **`random`** (local/test only).

## What RUTH is

A Teleport access-request plugin (Go) that:
1. Watches Teleport for pending access requests.
2. Scores each request via deterministic rules + an AI assessment.
3. Auto-approves requests below `risk.ticket_threshold`.
4. Files a Jira ITSM ticket and holds the Teleport request `PENDING` for the rest, polling Jira until an SRE resolves the ticket.
5. Maintains a per-user reputation score that only goes down, exported as an OTLP gauge for Datadog dashboards.

## Architecture

```
cmd/ruth/main.go      entry point; sets up signal context + slog JSON handler
config.go             TOML loader: applyDefaults() THEN unmarshal THEN applyEnv() THEN validate()
env.go                reflection-based RUTH_SECTION_FIELD env overrides; maps & slices skipped
app.go                watcher + ITSM poller under errgroup, with telemetry-aware shutdown grace
ai/provider.go        Provider interface, system prompt, JSON parser
ai/bedrock.go         bedrockruntime:Converse; default AWS chain + optional profile/role_arn
ai/random.go          test-only fabricated assessments (with optional seed)
risk/score.go         deterministic + AI components, off-hours, escalation detection
risk/risk.go          tier table, escalation threshold resolution
jira/itsm.go          create ticket, poll status, JQL-based restart rehydration
reputation/           per-user store with atomic JSON file persistence
telemetry/            OTLP/gRPC meter, ruth.user.reputation observable gauge
local/                docker-compose stack for end-to-end local testing
```

## Coding conventions

- **Go std lib first.** Pull a third-party dep only if std-lib code would be significantly larger.
- **Logging**: `slog` JSON to stderr. Never `fmt.Println` or `log.Printf` in production paths. Debug-only details (e.g. Jira request bodies) must gate on `slog.Default().Enabled(ctx, slog.LevelDebug)` so they don't run on every request.
- **Tests**: run with `-race` during development. Tests live next to code; mocks via interfaces only when needed.
- **No slang** in source code, AI system prompts, or Jira ticket text. The user has corrected this before. Use neutral language ("teleport", "access request"), not project-internal nicknames.
- **Concrete returns, interface params** when it makes sense — small interfaces, no premature abstraction.
- **Inline comments**: only when the *why* is non-obvious. Don't restate what the code says.

## Non-obvious design decisions (read these before refactoring)

### Config: defaults FIRST, then TOML, then env
`config.go:LoadConfig` calls `applyDefaults()` *before* `toml.Unmarshal`. This is intentional. The reverse order conflates "unset" with "explicit zero" and silently resurrects defaults for fields the user meant to disable (e.g. `reputation.penalty_missing_custx = 0`). Don't flip the order. Tests in `config_test.go` lock this behavior.

### `pending` map is the dedup source of truth
`app.go:reserveOrSkip` claims a slot for the request id atomically *before* launching the handler goroutine. The same map then records the ticket key on success. One source of truth — don't add a parallel "in flight" set. The deferred `releasePending` only fires if the handler doesn't successfully record a ticket, so failures retry naturally on the next OpPut.

### Reputation persist holds the write lock through fsync+rename
`reputation.persistLocked` keeps `s.mu` held across the whole tmp-write → fsync → rename sequence. Releasing the lock around file I/O lets two concurrent `apply` calls each snapshot independently and the slower `os.Rename` lands last, silently overwriting newer state. This was a bugbot finding — don't "optimize" it back.

### Jira rehydration regex tolerates wiki-bold markers
`reqIDRE = ` `Teleport Request ID:[^A-Za-z0-9-]*([A-Za-z0-9-]+)` — the character class between the colon and the capture is deliberately permissive because `buildDescription` writes `* *Teleport Request ID:* %s` (Jira wiki bold). A naive `\s*` regex matches nothing in the stored description and silently breaks restart rehydration. Don't tighten it.

### OTel exporter needs a shutdown grace period
A coordinator goroutine waits for the signal context, then sleeps `telemetry.shutdown_grace` (default `2s`, set `0s` to skip) before cancelling the watcher/poller errgroup. This lets the OTLP periodic reader finish an in-flight export instead of logging `context canceled`. Don't bolt watcher/poller directly to the signal context.

### `submit` tool generates a fresh UUID per run
`cmd/submit` uses `uuid.New()` per invocation; Teleport rejects duplicate request IDs, so a hardcoded UUID would break the documented "run it again with a different reason" flow.

### Bedrock auth chain
Default AWS credential chain (IRSA / Pod Identity / env / `~/.aws/credentials`) covers production. `profile` and `role_arn` are opt-in for local dev and cross-account AssumeRole. Don't add per-credential plumbing unless asked.

### AI system prompt is prompt-injection hardened
The "abuela" persona in `ai/provider.go:SystemPrompt` treats free-form request reasons as untrusted input. Injection attempts must drive `anomalies` up, never lower scores. If editing the prompt, preserve the security rules block and the calibration examples — they were tuned deliberately. The structured fields (User, Roles, Resources, Contains CUSTX) are authoritative; prose claims like "this is read-only" are not.

## Common commands

```sh
# build + test
go build ./...
go test -race ./...

# run against the local docker-compose stack (after ./local/bootstrap.sh)
go run ./cmd/ruth --config local/ruth.toml

# fire a synthetic request through the local stack
go run ./cmd/submit --reason "CUSTX-1234 reason text"

# dry-run mode (no Teleport reviews, no Jira tickets)
RUTH_DRY_RUN=true go run ./cmd/ruth --config /etc/ruth/ruth.toml
```

## Local test harness (`local/`)

Single-node Teleport in docker-compose, OTel collector with debug exporter, and a `random` AI provider so you don't need real Bedrock or Jira credentials. `risk.ticket_threshold` can be cranked to `101` to exercise reputation scoring without hitting Jira. Identity files are TTL 24h — re-run `./local/bootstrap.sh` when they expire.

`ruth.toml` (at repo root, gitignored) is the user's personal local config and may drift from `ruth.toml.example`. Don't edit it without asking.

## What NOT to do

- Don't reintroduce the Anthropic provider, the webhook provider, or the `TV_` env-var prefix without explicit instruction.
- Don't `fmt.Println` for debugging — use `slog.DebugContext`.
- Don't add slang ("sus", "fr", "vibe", etc.) to code, prompts, or ticket text.
- Don't loosen the security rules in the AI system prompt.
- Don't reorder `applyDefaults` / `toml.Unmarshal` / `applyEnv`.
- Don't release the reputation write lock around file I/O.
- Don't rename the project again. Once was enough.

## What RUTH is

A Teleport access-request plugin (Go) that:
1. Watches Teleport for pending access requests.
2. Scores each request via deterministic rules + an AI assessment.
3. Auto-approves requests below `risk.ticket_threshold`.
4. Files a Jira ITSM ticket and holds the Teleport request `PENDING` for the rest, polling Jira until an SRE resolves the ticket.
5. Maintains a per-user reputation score that only goes down, exported as an OTLP gauge for Datadog dashboards.

## Architecture

```
cmd/ruth/main.go      entry point; sets up signal context + slog JSON handler
config.go             TOML loader: applyDefaults() THEN unmarshal THEN applyEnv() THEN validate()
env.go                reflection-based RUTH_SECTION_FIELD env overrides; maps & slices skipped
app.go                watcher + ITSM poller under errgroup, with telemetry-aware shutdown grace
ai/provider.go        Provider interface, system prompt, JSON parser
ai/bedrock.go         bedrockruntime:Converse; default AWS chain + optional profile/role_arn
ai/random.go          test-only fabricated assessments (with optional seed)
risk/score.go         deterministic + AI components, off-hours, escalation detection
risk/risk.go          tier table, escalation threshold resolution
jira/itsm.go          create ticket, poll status, JQL-based restart rehydration
reputation/           per-user store with atomic JSON file persistence
telemetry/            OTLP/gRPC meter, ruth.user.reputation observable gauge
local/                docker-compose stack for end-to-end local testing
```

## Coding conventions

- **Go std lib first.** Pull a third-party dep only if std-lib code would be significantly larger.
- **Logging**: `slog` JSON to stderr. Never `fmt.Println` or `log.Printf` in production paths. Debug-only details (e.g. Jira request bodies) must gate on `slog.Default().Enabled(ctx, slog.LevelDebug)` so they don't run on every request.
- **Tests**: run with `-race` during development. Tests live next to code; mocks via interfaces only when needed.
- **No slang** in source code, AI system prompts, or Jira ticket text. The user has corrected this before. Use neutral language ("teleport", "access request"), not project-internal nicknames.
- **Concrete returns, interface params** when it makes sense — small interfaces, no premature abstraction.
- **Inline comments**: only when the *why* is non-obvious. Don't restate what the code says.

## Non-obvious design decisions (read these before refactoring)

### Config: defaults FIRST, then TOML, then env
`config.go:LoadConfig` calls `applyDefaults()` *before* `toml.Unmarshal`. This is intentional. The reverse order conflates "unset" with "explicit zero" and silently resurrects defaults for fields the user meant to disable (e.g. `reputation.penalty_missing_custx = 0`). Don't flip the order. Tests in `config_test.go` lock this behavior.

### `pending` map is the dedup source of truth
`app.go:reserveOrSkip` claims a slot for the request id atomically *before* launching the handler goroutine. The same map then records the ticket key on success. One source of truth — don't add a parallel "in flight" set. The deferred `releasePending` only fires if the handler doesn't successfully record a ticket, so failures retry naturally on the next OpPut.

### Reputation persist holds the write lock through fsync+rename
`reputation.persistLocked` keeps `s.mu` held across the whole tmp-write → fsync → rename sequence. Releasing the lock around file I/O lets two concurrent `apply` calls each snapshot independently and the slower `os.Rename` lands last, silently overwriting newer state. This was a bugbot finding — don't "optimize" it back.

### Jira rehydration regex tolerates wiki-bold markers
`reqIDRE = ` `Teleport Request ID:[^A-Za-z0-9-]*([A-Za-z0-9-]+)` — the character class between the colon and the capture is deliberately permissive because `buildDescription` writes `* *Teleport Request ID:* %s` (Jira wiki bold). A naive `\s*` regex matches nothing in the stored description and silently breaks restart rehydration. Don't tighten it.

### OTel exporter needs a shutdown grace period
A coordinator goroutine waits for the signal context, then sleeps `telemetry.shutdown_grace` (default `2s`, set `0s` to skip) before cancelling the watcher/poller errgroup. This lets the OTLP periodic reader finish an in-flight export instead of logging `context canceled`. Don't bolt watcher/poller directly to the signal context.

### `submit` tool generates a fresh UUID per run
`cmd/submit` uses `uuid.New()` per invocation; Teleport rejects duplicate request IDs, so a hardcoded UUID would break the documented "run it again with a different reason" flow.

### Bedrock auth chain
Default AWS credential chain (IRSA / Pod Identity / env / `~/.aws/credentials`) covers production. `profile` and `role_arn` are opt-in for local dev and cross-account AssumeRole. Don't add per-credential plumbing unless asked.

### AI system prompt is prompt-injection hardened
The "abuela" persona in `ai/provider.go:SystemPrompt` treats free-form request reasons as untrusted input. Injection attempts must drive `anomalies` up, never lower scores. If editing the prompt, preserve the security rules block and the calibration examples — they were tuned deliberately. The structured fields (User, Roles, Resources, Contains CUSTX) are authoritative; prose claims like "this is read-only" are not.

go test -race ./...
